## Definitions

- [passage] `planCacheKey` is a hash of the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape), further distinguished by any available indexes for the shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, planCacheKey
- [passage] A query shape hash is a string that uniquely identifies the query shape. An example query shape hash is `"F42757F1AEB68B4C5A6DE6182B29B01947C829C926BCC01226BDA4DDE799766C"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#set-query-settings-by-passing-in-a-query-shape-hash · keywords: query settings, query shape
- [passage] In the classic multi-planner, the winning plan is the query plan that produces the most results during the trial period while performing the least amount of work. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: query planner
- [passage] - Knobs that are not marked as settable through query settings — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query settings
- [passage] This parameter is not configurable with query settings. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: query settings
- [passage] - `$planCacheStats` is not allowed in: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#restrictions · keywords: plan cache, $planCacheStats

## Structure and components

- [fact] The settings document accepts indexHints, queryFramework (classic or sbe), reject, comment (8.0.4 and 8.1+), and in 9.0 queryKnobs (per-shape server parameter overrides, merged not replaced) and maxTimeMS (takes precedence over command-level maxTimeMS). Query knobs are part of the plan cache key; an FCV downgrade from 9.0 removes knobs and they are not restored on re-upgrade. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md · keywords: $currentOp, hint, index, plan cache, query settings, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] Index filters are set with the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command and determine which indexes the planner evaluates for a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape). A plan cache query shape consists of a combination of query, sort, and projection specifications. If an index filter exists for a given query shape, the planner only considers those indexes specified in the filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape, planCacheSetFilter
- [fact] If an index filter exists for the query shape, MongoDB ignores hint(). Cluster query settings also take precedence: index hints in command fields are ignored if a matching query setting already contains index hints. Index hints do not affect query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md · keywords: hint, index, query settings, query shape, hint() and Index Forcing · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md
- [passage] The [`dropIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropindexes.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.dropIndexes) operation only kills queries that are using the index being dropped. This may include queries considering the index as part of [query planning.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md#kill-related-queries-only · keywords: $indexStats, index, query planner, dropIndexes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [passage] - Cluster query settings take precedence over query settings or index hints passed as a command field. MongoDB ignores index hints in command fields if a matching query setting already contains index hints. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#behavior · keywords: hint, index, query settings
- [fact] Changing any shape component (e.g. the sort field from totalNumber to price) yields a different queryShapeHash and planCacheShapeHash; changing only literal values (dates) does not. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, the pre-existing query shape is renamed to the plan cache query shape, and the queryHash field is renamed planCacheShapeHash. For the components of a command that differentiate plan cache query shapes, see the plan cache query shape definition. MongoDB 8.0 uses the new query shape and the existing plan cache query shape as shown on this page. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md
- [passage] the overall structure of the find, aggregation, and distinct commands, which support a wider range of query shapes than the existing plan cache query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape
- [passage] - the overall structure of the `find`, `aggregation`, and `distinct` commands, which support a wider range of query shapes than the existing plan cache query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md · keywords: plan cache, query shape, find, aggregation, distinct
- [statement] Hinting a partial index limits results to documents matching its filter expression; the index becomes part of the query's semantics. — https://dev.to/mongodb/hint-in-mongodb-is-different-that-sql-optimizer-hints-they-force-indexes-4c33 · keywords: hint, index, hint() and Index Forcing
- [passage] Contains information on the selection of the query plan by the query optimizer. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: query optimization, query planner
- [passage] Optional. A flag that determines whether the index is hidden from the query planner. A hidden index is not evaluated as part of query plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes/ · keywords: index, query planner
- [passage] Hides an existing index from the query planner. An index hidden from the query planner is not evaluated as part of query plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex/ · keywords: index, query planner
- [passage] The number of queries that contain the `_id` field. For these queries, MongoDB uses the default index on the `_id` field and skips all query plan analysis. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: index, query planner, _id
- [passage] Hides an existing index from the query planner. An [index hidden from the query planner](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md#std-label-index-type-hidden) is not evaluated as part of query plan selection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.hideIndex.md#definition · keywords: index, query planner
- [passage] If you count the number of documents in the `movies` collection and include a hint that specifies that sparse index, the operation returns only the documents that contain the `rated` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: hint, index, movies, rated
- [passage] The `orders` collection contains the following index filters: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md#clear-specific-index-filter-on-collection · keywords: index, query settings, orders
- [passage] The array of documents that contain the index filter information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheListFilters.md#output · keywords: index, query settings
- [passage] Contains metrics related to CBR when it is used during query planning. CBR evaluates multiple query plans and selects the most efficient plan based on estimated costs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query planner
- [passage] Messages related to queries, including query planner activities. To specify the log level for QUERY components, set the systemLog.component.query.verbosity parameter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: query planner
- [passage] Messages related to queries, including query planner activities. To specify the log level for [`QUERY`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#mongodb-data-QUERY) components, set the [`systemLog.component.query.verbosity`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-systemLog.component.query.verbosity) parameter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#components · keywords: query planner, QUERY, systemLog.component.query.verbosity
- [passage] When you downgrade the FCV from `9.0` to an earlier version, a migration updates the stored query settings. The migration removes every knob whose minimum FCV exceeds the target version and deletes any settings entry that still contains only default values. Re-upgrading to `9.0` does not restore the removed knobs. You must re-apply them with `setQuerySettings`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: query settings, 9.0, setQuerySettings

## How it works

- [passage] - When an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) exists for the query shape, MongoDB ignores the [`hint()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#behavior · keywords: hint, index, query planner, query settings, query shape, hint()
- [fact] planSummary alone does not show whether planning was expensive. Profiler entries carry fromMultiPlanner (true only when multiple candidate plans were evaluated) and replanned (true only when a cached plan was evicted and re-evaluated); both are omitted when false, e.g. for plan-cache hits. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, plan cache, query planner, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [passage] Because index filters override the expected behavior of the planner as well as the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method, use index filters sparingly. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: hint, index, query planner, query settings, hint()
- [fact] Classic caching keys on a broadly parameterized query shape and stores only the index choice. SBE caching keys on a more conservative shape and stores a full SBE plan. SBE does not parameterize arrays, so find({a:'foo',b:[1]}) and find({a:'bar',b:[2]}) share a classic key but not an SBE key, and each new array value causes a miss and another multi-plan. SERVER-89436 (Needs Scheduling, no fix version) proposes layering the classic cache behind the SBE cache. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-89436 · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] Because the values in the `query` predicate are insignificant in determining the plan cache query shape, the following command would also remove the second index filter: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md#clear-specific-index-filter-on-collection · keywords: index, plan cache, query settings, query shape, query
- [passage] Number of slot-based execution engine query plans that were not found in the query cache because the query is ineligible for caching. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#plancache · keywords: plan cache, query planner, slot-based execution engine
- [passage] The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) typically selects the optimal index for a specific operation. However, you can force MongoDB to use a specific index using the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method. Use [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) to support performance testing or when you are querying a field that appears in several indexes to ensure that MongoDB uses the correct index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#use-index-hints · keywords: hint, index, query optimization, query planner, hint() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/
- [fact] A hinted sparse index is used even when it would omit documents: the planner normally avoids a sparse index that gives incomplete results, but an explicit hint forces it and the query returns only documents containing the field. A hinted countDocuments with an empty predicate on a sparse index returns an incorrect count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/index-sparse/ · keywords: hint, index, query planner, hint() and Index Forcing
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 6.0.7, if a usable clustered index exists, the MongoDB query planner evaluates the clustered index against secondary indexes in the query planning process. When a query uses a clustered index, MongoDB performs a [bounded collection scan.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-bounded-collection-scan) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#behavior · keywords: database profiler, index, query planner
- [passage] Removes [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) on a collection. Although index filters only exist for the duration of the server process and do not persist after shutdown, you can also clear existing index filters with the [`planCacheClearFilters`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancacheclearfilters.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheClearFilters) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md#definition · keywords: index, query planner, query settings, planCacheClearFilters · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md
- [passage] Number of classic execution engine query plans that were not found in the query cache because the query is ineligible for caching. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#plancache · keywords: plan cache, query planner
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `index` | string or document | The index to "hint" or force MongoDB to use when performing the query. Specify the index either by the index name or by the index specification document. You can also specify `{ $natural : 1 }` to force the query to perform a forwards collection scan, or `{ $natural : -1 }` for a reverse collection scan. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#definition · keywords: database profiler, hint, index, { $natural : 1 }, { $natural : -1 }
- [statement] Hinted index is the only index used, with no fallback to another index or collection scan; hinting by key pattern fails when several indexes share that pattern, so hint by name. min() and max() require a hint. — https://dev.to/mongodb/hint-in-mongodb-is-different-that-sql-optimizer-hints-they-force-indexes-4c33 · keywords: database profiler, hint, index, hint() and Index Forcing
- [passage] As with any hash function, two different query shapes may result in the same hash value. However, the occurrence of hash collisions between different query shapes is unlikely. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancacheshapehash · keywords: plan cache, query shape
- [passage] See [Plan Cache Flushes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-plan-cache-flushes) for additional scenarios that trigger changes to the plan cache. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plan-cache-entry-state · keywords: plan cache, query planner
- [passage] fromPlanCache is true when the query planner is able to use a plan from the plan cache. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: plan cache, query planner
- [passage] Call this method on a query to override MongoDB's default index selection and [query optimization process](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization). Use [`db.collection.getIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.getindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.getIndexes) to return the list of current indexes on a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#definition · keywords: index, query optimization, query planner, db.collection.getIndexes()
- [passage] When evaluating the clauses in the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) expression, MongoDB's query optimizer considers which indexes are available that could help satisfy clauses of the [`$and`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#mongodb-query-op.-and) expression when [selecting the best plan to execute.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/and.md#behavior · keywords: index, query optimization, query planner, $and
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, if the FCV (feature compatibility version) is 8.3 or later, MongoDB backfills the `representativeQuery` field for query settings that you set with a query shape hash. When MongoDB runs a query that matches the query shape, it schedules the backfill. The backfill requires no action from you. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#set-query-settings-by-passing-in-a-query-shape-hash · keywords: query settings, query shape, representativeQuery
- [passage] Because `showDebugQueryShape` is `true`, the `debugQueryShape` document is included in the output. You can use the `queryShapeHash` identifier to locate the query settings. `queryShapeHash` and `debugQueryShape` are highlighted in this output: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querySettings.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: query settings, query shape, showDebugQueryShape, true, debugQueryShape, queryShapeHash
- [fact] Classic multi-planning picks the winner as the plan that returns the most results in the trial period while doing the least work. The winner is stored in the plan cache and reused for queries with the same plan cache query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/ · keywords: plan cache, query shape, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] For example, the following query causes MongoDB to use the `timestamp_1_metadata.sensorId_1` index: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#specify-index-hints-for-time-series-collections · keywords: hint, index, timestamp_1_metadata.sensorId_1
- [fact] Per SERVER-90880, queries run in SBE use the classic plan cache by default; the SBE plan cache is used only when featureFlagSbeFull is on. In 8.0 only $group/$lookup-type queries tend to run in SBE. — https://jira.mongodb.com/browse/SERVER-90880 · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] When you sort based on an array field that is indexed with a [multikey index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multikey), the query plan includes an [in-memory sort](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-in-memory-sort) stage unless both of the following are true: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#sorting · keywords: index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sort-results-with-indexes.md
- [passage] Index properties affect how the query planner uses an index and how indexed documents are stored. You can specify index properties as optional parameters when you create an index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-properties.md · keywords: index, query planner
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.3, multi-planning with a cost-based ranker backup is the default plan selection mechanism for eligible queries. For a short trial period, the multi-planner attempts to find a plan capable of returning a result within the timeframe. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#query-plan-options · keywords: query planner
- [passage] Index hints cause MongoDB to use a specific index for a query. Some operations on time series collections can only take advantage of an index if that index is specified in a hint. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#specify-index-hints-for-time-series-collections · keywords: hint, index
- [passage] If you include a [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) that specifies a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when you perform a [`count()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.count.md#mongodb-method-cursor.count) of all documents in a collection (i.e. with an empty query predicate), the sparse index is used even if the sparse index results in an incorrect count. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: hint, index, hint(), count()
- [passage] Index filters exist for the duration of the server process and do not persist after shutdown. MongoDB also provides a command to manually remove filters. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, query settings
- [passage] fromMultiPlanner is true when the query planner evaluates multiple plans before choosing the winning execution plan for the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query planner
- [passage] The number of queries that exceeded the threshold that the [`maxEstimatedScanBytes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.maxEstimatedScanBytes) parameter sets but that the server ran anyway because a `$natural` hint overrode the rejection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: hint, maxEstimatedScanBytes, $natural
- [passage] When using [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe), the `$planCacheStats` stage omits operations against encrypted collections, even though the operations are cached as normal. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#redaction · keywords: plan cache, $planCacheStats
- [passage] When the `allHosts` option is set to `false`, [`$planCacheStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-planCacheStats) follows the [read preference](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/read-preference.md#std-label-read-preference) in selecting the host(s) from which to return the plan cache information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#read-preference · keywords: plan cache, allHosts, false, $planCacheStats
- [passage] Each field has the form `{ "value": <value>, "source": <string> }`. When you set a query knob with the [`setQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) command, MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"querySettings"`. When you set a query knob with [`setParameter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setparameter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setParameter), MongoDB sets the `source` value to `"setParameter"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#query-knobs · keywords: query settings, { "value": <value>, "source": <string> }, setQuerySettings, source, "querySettings", setParameter · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] Set an [index filter](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters) for a collection. If an index filter already exists for the [plan cache query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-plan-cache-query-shape), the command overrides the previous index filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md#definition · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query settings, query shape
- [passage] To choose the best query plan, the query optimizer evaluates the [`indexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachelistfilters.md#mongodb-data-planCacheListFilters.filters.indexes) *and* the collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheListFilters.md#output · keywords: database profiler, index, query optimization, query planner, query settings, indexes
- [passage] To provide more insight into the [query plan cache](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md), MongoDB offers the `planCacheKey`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: plan cache, query planner, planCacheKey
- [passage] To see the query shapes for which cached query plans exist, see [Examples.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#std-label-planCacheStats-examples) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClear.md#command-fields · keywords: query planner, query shape
- [passage] Use `$natural` in conjunction with `cursor.hint()` to perform a collection scan to return documents in [natural order.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-natural-order) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#natural · keywords: database profiler, hint, $natural, cursor.hint()
- [passage] To add query settings for a query shape, use setQuerySettings. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query settings, query shape
- [passage] To verify that the slot-based execution engine is used, run the aggregation with the `explain` option. This option outputs information on the aggregation's query plan. For more information on using `explain` with aggregations, see [Return Information on Aggregation Pipeline Operation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md#std-label-example-aggregate-method-explain-option) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#slot-based-query-execution-engine-pipeline-optimizations · keywords: query planner, slot-based execution engine, explain
- [passage] To return plan cache information for a particular query hash, the [`$planCacheStats`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/plancachestats.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-planCacheStats) stage can be followed by a [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) on the `planCacheKey` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/planCacheStats.md#find-cache-entry-details-for-a-query-hash · keywords: plan cache, query shape, $planCacheStats, $match, planCacheKey
- [passage] To delete query settings, you must provide either a [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) hash string or a query shape to `removeQuerySettings`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removeQuerySettings.md#definition · keywords: query settings, query shape, removeQuerySettings
- [passage] To find a hash string or query shape, you can use a [`$querySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querysettings.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-querySettings) stage in an aggregation pipeline. The hash string is named `queryShapeHash` in the `$querySettings` output. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removeQuerySettings.md#definition · keywords: query settings, query shape, $querySettings, queryShapeHash
- [passage] To locate the query settings to delete, use the `queryShapeHash` string in this output: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removeQuerySettings.md#examples · keywords: query settings, query shape, queryShapeHash
- [passage] To hide an index, you must have [featureCompatibilityVersion](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setfeaturecompatibilityversion.md#std-label-view-fcv) set to `7.0` or greater. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md#hide-an-index-from-the-query-planner · keywords: index, query planner, 7.0
- [passage] To see the index used, run [`explain`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/explain.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.explain) on the operation: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/findAndModify.md#specify-hint-for-findandmodify-operations · keywords: hint, index, explain
- [passage] To force MongoDB to use a particular index, use cursor.hint() (mongosh method) when testing indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-rule/ · keywords: hint, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/equality-sort-range-guideline.md
- [passage] To use an index with the [`max()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md#mongodb-method-cursor.max) method, you must use the [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) method to specify the index you want to use, except when the [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) query is an equality condition on the `_id` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#definition · keywords: hint, index, max(), hint(), find(), _id · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md
- [passage] To obtain the correct count of the number of documents in the `movies` collection, do not [`hint()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) with a [sparse index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) when performing a count of all documents in a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-and-incomplete-results · keywords: hint, index, movies, hint()
- [passage] To use the sparse index, explicitly specify the index with [`hint()`:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.hint.md#mongodb-method-cursor.hint) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#sparse-index-on-a-collection-cannot-return-complete-results · keywords: hint, index, hint()
- [passage] To view the query plan, click Explain in the query bar. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan/ · keywords: query planner
- [passage] To return information on [query plans](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) and execution statistics of the query plans, MongoDB provides the following methods: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md · keywords: query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] To bypass rejection for a specific query, add a `$natural` hint to the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#general-parameters · keywords: hint, $natural
- [passage] To remove query settings, use [`removeQuerySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/removequerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.removeQuerySettings). To see current query settings, use a [`$querySettings`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querysettings.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-querySettings) stage in an aggregation pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#definition · keywords: query settings, removeQuerySettings, $querySettings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md
- [passage] To add query settings and explore examples, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.distinct.md#query-settings · keywords: query settings, setQuerySettings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.aggregate.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/aggregate.md
- [passage] To delete query settings, use removeQuerySettings. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query settings
- [passage] To retrieve query settings, use a $querySettings stage in an aggregation pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query settings

- [passage] To set the `reject` field, use `setQuerySettings`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: query settings, reject, setQuerySettings

## Measurements and reference values

- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, the [plan cache](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) will save full `plan cache` entries only if the cumulative size of the `plan caches` for all collections is lower than 0.5 GB. When the cumulative size of the `plan caches` for all collections exceeds this threshold, additional `plan cache` entries are stored without the following debug information: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plan-cache-debug-info-size-limit · keywords: plan cache, query planner, plan caches
- [passage] - A percentage of the system's total physical memory to allocate for the plan cache. For example, `"8.5%"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#slot-based-execution-parameters · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, "8.5%"
- [passage] - The exact amount of data to allocate for the plan cache in either `MB` or `GB`. For example, `"100MB"` or `"1GB"`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#slot-based-execution-parameters · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, MB, GB, "100MB", "1GB"
- [fact] The classic multi-planner's trial is bounded to the larger of 10,000 storage reads or 30% of the collection (internalQueryPlanEvaluationCollFraction). SERVER-62981, fixed in 5.2.1/5.3.0, proposed internalQueryPlanEvaluationCollFractionSbe (default 0, meaning 10,000 reads per candidate) for SBE. The shipped SBE default was not confirmed. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-62981 · keywords: plan cache, slot-based execution engine, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [statement] Full $planCacheStats debug info (createdFromQuery, cachedPlan, creationExecStats, candidatePlanScores) is kept only while total plan cache size across all collections is under 0.5 GB (since 5.0). Since 6.3 the planCacheSize parameter sets the cache size, with a default of 5% of memory (per Percona). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/core/query-plans/ · keywords: plan cache, Query Planning and Plan Cache

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `distinct` | string | The name of the collection to query for distinct values. | | `key` | string | The field for which to return distinct values. | | `query` | document | Optional. A query that specifies the documents from which to retrieve the distinct values. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). Available for read operations on the [`primary`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-states.md#mongodb-replstate-replstate.PRIMARY) only.; [`"snapshot"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-snapshot.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-snapshot-). Available for [multi-document transactions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md#std-label-transactions) and certain read operations outside of multi-document transactions. For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) | | `collation` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | | `hint` | string or document | Optional. Specify the index name, either as a string or a document. If specified, the query planner only considers plans using the hinted index. For more details, see [Specify an Index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#std-label-index-example) **New in version 7.1** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/distinct.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, hint, index, query planner, query settings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/count.md
- [fact] Settings can be set by passing a full find/distinct/aggregate command plus $db, or by passing an existing query shape hash string; the hash is obtainable from $querySettings (queryShapeHash), the profiler, or slow query logs. Hash-created settings lack representativeQuery until 8.3 (FCV 8.3+), which backfills it asynchronously, best effort. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md · keywords: database profiler, hint, index, query settings, query shape, Query Settings and Persistent Index Hints (8.0)
- [fact] Explain exposes queryShapeHash and planCacheShapeHash at the top level; SERVER-91954 added it (fixed in 8.0.4 and 8.1.0-rc0, resolved 2024-09-20). Before that, the hash was only available from the slow query log/profiler or via setQuerySettings plus $querySettings. — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-91954 · keywords: database profiler, plan cache, query settings, query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [statement] A replanning loop occurs when data changes faster than the planner adapts. Causes: data-dependent filter values, non-selective indexes, near-tied plans, rapid cardinality change (bulk insert/delete, TTL, capped overwrite), and $or/$in/$regex with variable item counts. Diagnose with slow-log fields replanned: true, replanReason, planningTimeMicros, fromMultiPlanner, queryHash and planCacheKey. — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/ · keywords: index, plan cache, query planner, query shape, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [fact] Mitigations for plan instability: add more selective indexes, avoid generic queries, cap $or/$in value counts, use hint() as a short-term stabilizer, or use 8.0 query settings for a cluster-wide hint. Index filters (planCacheSetFilter) are deprecated from 8.0 in favor of query settings, and they do not persist across shutdown. — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-query-plan-cache-explained-performance-pitfalls-and-re-planning/ · keywords: hint, index, plan cache, query settings, Query Planning and Plan Cache
- [passage] Query settings have more functionality than index filters. Also, index filters aren't persistent and you cannot easily create index filters for all cluster nodes. To add query settings and explore examples, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, query settings, plan cache, query shape, setQuerySettings · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.stats.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `query` | document | Optional. The query predicate of the plan cache query shape. Only the structure of the predicate, including the field names, are significant to the shape; the values in the query predicate are insignificant. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The projection associated with the plan cache query shape. | | `sort` | document | Optional. The sort associated with the plan cache query shape. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | | `collation` | document | Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClear.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, plan cache, query shape, query, projection

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `planCacheSetFilter` | string | The name of the collection for the index filter. | | `query` | document | The query predicate for the index filter. Only the predicate structure, including the field names, is used in the index filter. The field values in the query predicate are not used. Therefore, the query predicate in an index filter is used by similar queries that differ only in the field values. | | `sort` | document | Optional. The sort for the index filter. | | `projection` | document | Optional. The projection for the index filter. | | `collation` | document | Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. For descriptions of the fields, see [Collation Document.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation-document-fields) If the collation is unspecified but the collection has a default collation (see [`db.createCollection()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.createcollection.md#mongodb-method-db.createCollection)), the operation uses the collation specified for the collection. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, an index filter uses the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) previously set using the [`planCacheSetFilter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/plancachesetfilter.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.planCacheSetFilter) command. Starting in MongoDB 8.0, use query settings instead of adding [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters). Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. Query settings have more functionality than index filters. Also, index filters aren't persistent and you cannot easily create index filters for all cluster nodes. To add query settings and explore examples, see [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) | | `indexes` | array | An array of index filters for the specified plan cache query shape. Specify the index filters as one of these arrays: Index specification documents. For example, `[ { x : 1 }, ... ]`.; Index names. For example, `[ "x_1", ... ]`. The [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) uses either a collection scan or the index arrays for the query plan. If the specified indexes do not exist or are [hidden](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-hidden.md), the optimizer uses a collection scan. For multiple indexes with the same key pattern, you must specify the index as an array of names. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. - [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `find` | string | The name of the collection or [view](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/views.md#std-label-views-landing-page) to query. | | `filter` | document | Optional. Index specification. Specify either the index name as a string or the index key pattern. If specified, the query system only considers plans using the hinted index. With the following exception, `hint` is required if the command includes the `min` or `max` fields. `hint` is not required with `min` or `max` if the `filter` is an equality condition on the `_id` field `{ _id: <value> }`. | | `skip` | positive integer | Optional. Number of documents to skip. Defaults to 0. | | `limit` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents to return. If unspecified, then defaults to no limit. A limit of 0 is equivalent to setting no limit. | | `batchSize` | non-negative integer | Optional. The maximum number of documents that can be returned in each batch of a query result. By default, the `find` command has an initial `batchSize` of the lesser of `101` documents or 16 mebibytes (MiB) worth of documents. Subsequent batches have a maximum size of 16 MiB. This option can enforce a smaller limit than 16 MiB, but not a larger one. When set, the `batchSize` is the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB worth of documents. A `batchSize` of `0` means that the cursor is established, but no documents are returned in the first batch. Unlike the previous wire protocol version, a batchSize of 1 for the [`find`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.find) command does not close the cursor. To specify batch size for subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) operations, use [`batchSize()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.batchsize.md#mongodb-method-cursor.batchSize) in mongosh. | | `singleBatch` | boolean | Optional. Determines whether to close the cursor after the first batch. Defaults to false. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). Any comment set on a `find` command is inherited by any subsequent [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) commands run on the `find` cursor. | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies a time limit in milliseconds. If you do not specify a value for `maxTimeMS`, operations will not time out. A value of `0` explicitly specifies the default unbounded behavior. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their allotted time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp). MongoDB only terminates an operation at one of its designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) When specifying [`linearizable read concern`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-), always use `maxTimeMS` in case a majority of data bearing members are unavailable. `maxTimeMS` ensures that the operation does not block indefinitely and instead returns an error if the read concern cannot be fulfilled. [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) is unrelated to [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout). [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) limits processing time, while [`noCursorTimeout()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.nocursortimeout.md#mongodb-method-cursor.noCursorTimeout) prevents idle-time expiration. A cursor's idle time does not contribute to its processing time. | | `readConcern` | document | Optional. Specifies the [read concern.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-read-concern) The `readConcern` option has the following syntax: `readConcern: { level: <value> }` Possible read concern levels are: [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-). This is the default read concern level for read operations against the primary and secondaries.; [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-). Available for read operations against the primary and secondaries. [`"available"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-available.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-available-) behaves the same as [`"local"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-local.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-local-) against the primary and non-sharded secondaries. The query returns the instance's most recent data.; [`"majority"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-majority.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-majority-). Available for replica sets that use [WiredTiger storage engine.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger.md#std-label-storage-wiredtiger); [`"linearizable"`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern-linearizable.md#mongodb-readconcern-readconcern.-linearizable-). For more formation on the read concern levels, see [Read Concern Levels.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/read-concern.md#std-label-read-concern-levels) The [`getMore`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/getmore.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.getMore) command uses the `readConcern` level specified in the originating `find` command. | | `max` | document | Optional. Optional. Specifies the [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) to use for the operation. [Collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) allows users to specify language-specific rules for string comparison, such as rules for lettercase and accent marks. The collation option has the following syntax: `collation: { locale: <string>, caseLevel: <boolean>, caseFirst: <string>, strength: <int>, numericOrdering: <boolean>, alternate: <string>, maxVariable: <string>, backwards: <boolean> }` When specifying collation, the `locale` field is mandatory; all other collation fields are optional. If no collation is specified for the collection or for the operations, MongoDB uses the simple binary comparison used in prior versions for string comparisons. You cannot specify multiple collations for an operation. For example, you cannot specify different collations per field, or if performing a find with a sort, you cannot use one collation for the find and another for the sort. | | [allowDiskUse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-cmd-allowDiskUse) | boolean | Optional. Starting in MongoDB 6.0, if [`allowDiskUseByDefault`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.allowDiskUseByDefault) is set to `true` and the server requires more than 100 megabytes of memory for a pipeline execution stage, MongoDB automatically writes temporary files to disk unless the query specifies `{ allowDiskUse: false }`. Specifies a document with a list of variables. This allows you to improve command readability by separating the variables from the query text. The document syntax is: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` The variable is set to the value returned by the expression, and cannot be changed afterwards. To access the value of a variable in the command, use the double dollar sign prefix (`$$`) together with your variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example: `$$targetTotal`. To use a variable to filter results, you must access the variable within the [`$expr`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/expr.md#mongodb-query-op.-expr) operator. For a complete example using `let` and variables, see [Use Variables in `let`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#std-label-find-let-example) **New in version 5.0** | | `querySettings` | document | Optional. Query settings that apply only to this execution of the command. The `querySettings` document accepts the following fields: `indexHints`; `queryFramework`; `reject`; `comment`; `queryKnobs`; `maxTimeMS` For descriptions of these fields, see [Command Fields.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#std-label-setQuerySettings-fields) MongoDB doesn't store these settings on the cluster, and they don't apply to other queries with the same [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes). To set query settings that persist for a query shape, use [`setQuerySettings`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setquerysettings.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setQuerySettings) MongoDB combines the settings that you pass in the command with any query settings stored on the cluster for the same query shape. If both settings specify the same field, the stored cluster setting takes precedence. **New in version 9.0** | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/find.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, hint, index, query settings, query shape
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, use query settings instead of adding [index filters](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-index-filters). Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#index-filters · keywords: index, query planner, query settings, plan cache, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.stats.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheSetFilter.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/planCacheClearFilters.md
- [passage] | State | Description | | --- | --- | | [Missing](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-missing) | No entry for this shape exists in the cache. For a query, if the cache entry state for a plan cache query shape is [Missing:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-missing) Candidate plans are evaluated and a winning plan is selected.; The cache creates an entry for the plan cache query shape in state [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) with a value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan. | | [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) | The entry in the cache is a placeholder entry for this shape. That is, the planner has seen the shape, calculated a value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan and stored the shape placeholder entry but the plan cache query shape is **not** used to generate query plans. For a query, if the cache entry state for a shape is [Inactive:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) Candidate plans are evaluated and a winning plan is selected.; The selected plan's value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is compared to the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's. If the selected plan's value is:Less than or equal to the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's:The selected plan replaces the placeholder [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry and has an [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) state.If before the replacement happens, the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry becomes [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) (for example, due to another query operation), the newly active entry will only be replaced if its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is greater than the selected plan.; Greater than the [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry's:The [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) entry remains but its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan is incremented. | | [Active](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) | The entry in the cache is for the winning plan. The planner can use this entry to generate query plans. For a query, if the cache entry state for a shape is [Active:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-active) The active entry is used to generate query plans. The planner also evaluates the entry's performance and if its value that quantifies the amount of work required by the plan no longer meets the selection criterion, it will transition to [Inactive](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-cache-entry-inactive) state. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plan-cache-entry-state · keywords: plan cache, query planner, query shape
- [passage] Query knobs are part of the hashed query settings, so they are also part of the [plan cache key](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-plan-cache-key). If you change a knob value, MongoDB produces a new plan cache key, so the planner creates a fresh plan instead of reusing a stale cached plan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setQuerySettings.md#query-knobs · keywords: plan cache, query planner, query settings
- [passage] Prior to MongoDB 6.0.7, if a [secondary index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary-index) existed on a clustered collection and the secondary index was usable by your query, the query planner selected the secondary index instead of the clustered index by default. In MongoDB 6.1 and prior, to use the clustered index, you must provide a hint because the [query optimizer](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) does not automatically select the clustered index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/clustered-collections.md#behavior · keywords: hint, index, query optimization, query planner
- [passage] Unlike `planCacheShapeHash`, `planCacheKey` is a function of both the query shape and the currently available indexes for the shape. That is, if indexes that can support the query shape are added/dropped, the `planCacheKey` value may change whereas the `planCacheShapeHash` value would not change. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#plancachekey · keywords: index, plan cache, query shape, planCacheShapeHash, planCacheKey · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 8.0, add query settings for query shapes instead of index filters for collections. Index filters are deprecated starting in MongoDB 8.0. Query settings have more functionality than index filters, and index filters aren't persistent after cluster shutdown. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: index, query settings, query shape
- [passage] If one of the two boundaries is not specified, the query plan will be an index scan that is unbounded on one side. This may degrade performance compared to a query containing neither operator, or one that uses both operators to more tightly constrain the index scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.min.md#min-without-max · keywords: index, query planner · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.max.md
- [passage] | Parameter | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `unique` | boolean | Optional. Creates a unique index so that the collection will not accept insertion or update of documents where the index key value matches an existing value in the index. Specify `true` to create a unique index. The default value is `false`. The option is *unavailable* for [hashed indexes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-hashed.md#std-label-index-hashed-index) | | `name` | string | Optional.
